Title: The effects of maternal hyperoxia on fetal breathing movements, body movements and heart rate variation in growth retarded fetuses.
Journal: Early human development
Outcome: fetal breathing movements; body movements; heart rate variation
Evidence_Quote: The effect of hyperoxygenation on fetal breathing and body movements and on fetal heart rate was evaluated.

Title: Newborns' head orientation toward trains of brief sounds.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: head orientation
Evidence_Quote: Infants' responses to various trains of repeated 14-ms rattle sounds were compared with those to a 10-s rattle sound, known to elicit head orientation.

Title: Reorganization of auditory cortex after neonatal high frequency cochlear hearing loss.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: cochleotopic representation in cortex
Evidence_Quote: Cochleotopic representation in cortex (AI) is extensively reorganized in cats having neonatal, bilateral high frequency cochlear hearing loss.

Title: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation induces selective survival of spiral ganglion neurons in neonatally deafened cats.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation; ABR/FFR testing
Outcome: Selective spiral ganglion neuron survival in stimulated cochleas
Evidence_Quote: Profound hearing losses were documented by ABR and FFR (500 Hz) testing. At 9-17 weeks of age, the young deafened cats were unilaterally implanted with a multichannel scala tympani electrode. Six of the animals were chronically stimulated at 6 dB above electrically evoked ABR thresholds for 1 h/day for periods of 1 month or 3 months.

Title: Effects of neonatal deafening and chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation on the cochlear nucleus in cats.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: Cochlear nucleus spherical cell density, area and volume after deafening/stimulation
Evidence_Quote: The animals were stimulated daily (starting at 13-18 weeks of age), for a period of one hour, at 6 dB above the electrically evoked auditory brainstem response threshold.

Title: Methods for estimating infant thresholds.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: Threshold estimates compared across adaptive procedures and method of constant stimuli
Evidence_Quote: Detection thresholds for 1000-Hz, 16-ms tone bursts were estimated for 3- and 6-month-old infants and for young adults.

Title: Reduction and recovery of neuronal size in the cochlear nucleus of the chicken following aminoglycoside intoxication.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: cross-sectional area of neurons in nucleus magnocellularis
Evidence_Quote: The effect of aminoglycoside intoxication on the cross-sectional area of neurons in nucleus magnocellularis (NM) was studied in neonatal chickens.

Title: Rapid development of a sensory attribute in young chickens.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Background tone with frequency changes (habituation/peep-delay paradigm)
Outcome: Consistent frequency-change responses emerge within the first postnatal day
Evidence_Quote: Durations of these delays are used as measures of perceived difference between all possible pairs of five frequencies between 500 and 608 Hz.

Title: Microphonic versus end-tidal carbon dioxide nasal airflow detection in neonates with apnea.
Journal: Pediatrics
Outcome: respiration; apnea detection
Evidence_Quote: Analyses of 100 breaths from five patient samples during active and quiet sleep showed that there was no significant difference between microphone and expired CO2 recording of respiration.

Title: Increased heating by diagnostic ultrasound due to nonlinear propagation.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: temperature rise in tissue-mimicking gel (enhancement up to a factor of 3; max 2 degrees C)
Evidence_Quote: Measurements were made of the temperature rise in a sample of tissue-mimicking gel, caused by the application of 3.6-MHz focused ultrasonic beams for 3 min.

Title: Classification of audiograms by sequential testing using a dynamic Bayesian procedure.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: audiogram estimation
Evidence_Quote: A new method for estimating audiograms using behavioral responses is presented.

Title: Infant speech-sound discrimination in noise.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: Speech sounds (/ba/ vs /ga/) in noise at varied signal-to-noise ratios
Outcome: Discrimination performance vs S/N; infant S/N threshold 5.8 dB poorer than adults
Evidence_Quote: Variation in performance as a function of signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) was estimated by testing each infant at four S/N's (-8, 0, 8, and 16 dB).

Title: Development of temporal integration in newborn chickens.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Pure tones and bands of noise, 10-460 ms duration (temporal integration)
Outcome: Thresholds decrease approximately 6 dB per doubling of stimulus duration
Evidence_Quote: An adaptive procedure was used to estimate absolute thresholds of pure tones and bands of noise between 10 and 460 ms in duration.

Title: In vitro ultrasonic heating of fetal bone.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human fetal femurs (in vitro specimens, various gestational ages)
Stimulus_Type: 1 MHz continuous-wave ultrasound exposure (in vitro fetal bone heating)
Outcome: Temperature increase in fetal bone vs soft-tissue absorption values
Evidence_Quote: The temperature increase measured in vitro in human fetal femurs exposed to 1 MHz, continuous wave ultrasound at 37 degrees C is reported.

Title: Vocal fundamental frequency characteristics during the first two years of life.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: vocal fundamental frequency characteristics
Evidence_Quote: Vocal fundamental frequency (Fo) characteristics were sampled for a group of seven young children.

Title: Could temporal order differences underlie 2-month-olds' discrimination of English voicing contrasts?
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: [ba]-[pa] stimuli; [du]-[tu] stimuli; nonspeech formant onset time stimuli
Outcome: discrimination; perceptual category boundaries
Evidence_Quote: tests with 2-month-old infants using high amplitude sucking procedure yielded estimates of perceptual category boundaries at between 20 and 40 ms for all three stimulus series

Title: ABR threshold is a function of blood oxygen level.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: ABR testing under room air and hypoxic gas mixtures
Outcome: ABR threshold elevation of about 3.05 dB per mmHg decrease in PaO2 under hypoxia
Evidence_Quote: ABR threshold was an inverse function of blood O2 level with an approximate 3.05 dB elevation for every mmHg decrease in PaO2 (2.89 dB/% SaO2).

Title: Discrimination of frequency transitions by human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: difference limens for frequency transitions (~3%-4% for 300-ms sweeps; ~6%-7% for 50-ms sweeps)
Evidence_Quote: Difference limens (DLs) for linear frequency transitions using a 1.0-kHz pulsed-tone standard were obtained from 6- to 9-month-old human infants in a series of three experiments.

Title: Infants' monaural localization of sounds: effects of unilateral ear infection.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: sound localization
Evidence_Quote: Sound localization was measured using a two-alternative forced-choice procedure to examine infants' abilities to discriminate a sound shift of 8 degrees, 12 degrees, 16 degrees, and 20 degrees off midline and along the horizontal axis, either ipsilateral or contralateral to the infected ear.

Title: Recovery of auditory function following intense sound exposure in the neonatal chick.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: Threshold shift of 60 dB immediately after exposure; near-complete recovery by day 15
Evidence_Quote: One day old chicks were exposed to a 0.9 kHz tone for 48 h at 120 dB. At 0, 1, 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15 days after exposure, cochlear nucleus sound-evoked potentials were used to assess threshold sensitivity and frequency selectivity. Immediately after removal from the pure tone a threshold shift of 60 dB relative to age-matched controls was measured.

Title: Developmental changes in masked thresholds.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: listeners 6.5 months to 20.5 years of age
Stimulus_Type: Octave-band noises in broadband masker (masked thresholds)
Outcome: Masked thresholds decline exponentially with age
Evidence_Quote: Masked thresholds for octave-band noises with center frequencies of 0.4, 1, 2, 4, and 10 kHz and for a 1/3-octave-band noise centered at 10 kHz were obtained from listeners 6.5 months to 20.5 years of age at two levels of a broadband masker (0 and 10 dB/cycle).
